problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}+1?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y=3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/664a9c365070244d6c1e0047b140d9d108d9a03cf4fe32eec4694236e8740e8f.png)

- Reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,3)$ to $(0,-3)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/00256f0296c36170d317afc06316d7920f9b2a1f89dfa534eca91cb5e395b6ee.png)

- Then, vertically shift it by $1$ unit up to give $y=-3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{x}+1.$ The point $(0,-3)$ moves to $(0,-2)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938518/assets/662ad8370cf4c696bf831544bf425a28223a74a63cbf959521f69a7166b4dfc8.png)
